status: candidate / pending_human_review (model reading, round 21 second round; not an operator gate)
dataset_family: Shanghai community-screening cohorts, 1 Sep 2017 to 31 Aug 2018 (Shanghai University and the Shanghai Geriatric Institute of Chinese Medicine; ethics from Long Hua Hospital, 2017LCSY345). Cohort 1: four communities in Jiading district, 336 people (152 MCI / 184 NC per the methods and Table 1; the abstract swaps these to 184 MCI / 152 NC). Cohort 2: one community in Baoshan district, 92 people (44 MCI / 48 NC). No other corpus block reports these cohorts.
method_family: RBF-kernel SVM on MRMR-selected features from a single-electrode wearable EEG, eye tracking (saccade and gaze data, blink frequency and time, fixation time, sustained attention duration, LZC complexity), a 20-subtest neuropsychological battery and clinical variables. Four models were compared: clinical, NTB-only, 'single physiological test model' (EEG and ET together) and all combined. No model uses eye tracking alone, and the paper does not report which features MRMR kept.
what_it_shows:
Jiang J, Zhang J, Li C, Yu Z, Yan Z, Jiang J (2022), Brain Sciences 12:1149.
- The combined EEG+ET+NTB+clinical SVM reached AUC 0.9415 in Cohort 1 and 0.966 in Cohort 2.
- The 'single physiological test model' (EEG and ET together) reached AUC 0.9045 (Cohort 1) and 0.937 (Cohort 2), accuracy 81.4% and 87.0% (Tables 3-4).
- Eye tracking is never analysed or reported on its own. No ET feature, ET-only model, ET group difference or ET feature weight appears anywhere in the paper.
why:
IDENTITY. The PDF's title, authors (Juanjuan Jiang, Jieming Zhang, Chenyang Li, Zhihua Yu, Zhuangzhi Yan, Jiehui Jiang) and DOI 10.3390/brainsci12091149 match the block, whose header is the file name. I read the whole extract, pp.1-10, up to the reference list. Ligatures ('fi') in the extract are normalised in the quotes below.

STATED FORM, no. The statement concerns ocular channels. This study never isolates the ocular channel. Its only physiological comparison is the 'single physiological test model (EEG and ET)' (p.6), which joins a wearable EEG with eye tracking. Features were chosen by MRMR (p.4), and the paper never reports which features survived selection, so it does not even show that any eye-tracking feature entered a final model. The AUC of 0.90-0.94 therefore cannot be credited to eye-movement behaviour; it could come wholly from the EEG. The community setting and the second cohort bear on 'scalable', but only for the combined tool. To count this study for the ocular channel, one would have to credit an EEG+ET result to ET, and the source gives no basis for that. For that reason I score it no rather than partly.

The finder's reason also rests on Cohort 2 being a held-out validation. The paper says Cohort 2 was 'an independent test group' (p.6), but it also says 'We used the 5-fold cross-validation method to calculate the classification results' (p.6), and every Cohort-2 figure in Table 4 is printed as mean +/- SD, the format Table 2's footnote gives for five cross-validation folds. The paper therefore does not make clear that the Cohort-2 figures come from a model trained on Cohort 1 and applied once to Cohort 2.

Further problems in the source. These are my arithmetic, not the authors' statements:
(1) Cohort-2 age is 69.3 +/- 17.0 (NC, n = 48) against 76.5 +/- 11.3 (MCI, n = 44), with p = 0.783. A two-sample t-test on those printed values gives t of about 2.4, p of about 0.02, so the claim of no age difference in Cohort 2 (p.7) is not reproducible from Table 1.
(2) The Table 1 p-values for education and gender are swapped against the text: the text gives gender p = 0.541 and education p = 0.071, the table the reverse.
(3) The MCI inclusion criteria require 'intact general cognitive function confirmed by MoCA-B scores >=26' (p.6), yet MCI mean MoCA-B is 23.2 +/- 3.40 in Cohort 1 and 16.4 in Cohort 2 (Table 1).
(4) In Table 3 the NTB-only model has accuracy 75.6% with sensitivity 55.7% and specificity 71.2%. Accuracy above both is impossible for a single confusion matrix.
The authors concede a limited sample and a time-consuming protocol that reduces completion (p.10).

NARROWED FORM, no. The narrowed wording states that ocular measures show group-level associations with MCI or discriminate MCI. This paper reports no ocular measure's association with MCI and no ocular-only discrimination.

INDEPENDENCE. Shanghai community cohorts (Jiading, Baoshan). No shared sample, site or authors with P-5 (Chongqing/Wenzhou), P-952 (Shenzhen), P-966 (KIOM/GARD Korea) or P-105, or with the round-1 candidates. P-933 is also in Shanghai but comes from Ruijin Hospital, a different site with different authors. The same group's earlier EEG+ET work (ref [23], accuracy 81.5%) is not a corpus block. Not a preprint: a peer-reviewed MDPI article.

DEFECTS NOTED. The block's sample-size field, '184 MCI/152 NC', copies the abstract's swapped counts; the methods and Table 1 give 152 MCI / 184 NC. The registry Modality is 'EEG/MEG'; the paper is EEG + eye tracking + NTB.

quotes.quote: Cohort 1 as the training and validation group, includes184 MCI patients and 152 NC subjects. Cohort 2 as an independent test group, includes 44 MCI and 48 NC individuals.

ET data was divided into saccade data and gaze data. The association of gazes and saccades with specific regions on visual stimuli was examined. Then, visual scan parameters such as blink frequency, blink time, fixation time, and sustained attention duration were calculated. The nonlinear features of ET were extracted by LZC.

Cohort 1 was composed of 336 subjects from four communities in Jiading district, Shanghai, China, including 152 MCI patients and 184 normal controls (NC) subjects. Cohort 2 was composed of 44 MCI patients and 48 NC subjects from one community in Baoshan district, Shanghai, China.
the training and validation group to train the SVM classifier. Cohort 2 was used as an independent test group to verify the robustness of the classification results.

The classification results from four models were compared by using the SVM classifier, including (1) the clinical model (clinical variables including age, gender, educational level, MoCA-B, ACE-R), (2) the single neuropsychological test model (20 subtests of NTB showed in the Supplementary Material), (3) the single physiological test model (EEG and ET), and (4) the proposed tool model. We used the 5-fold cross-validation method to calculate the classification results.
